learningObjective: Analyze arithmetic intensity of tiled GEMM as a function of thread-block tile size.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a tiled GEMM with thread-block tile `BM × BN × BK`, per K-loop iteration the arithmetic intensity is BM*BN/(2*(BM+BN)) FLOPs/byte. Larger square tiles yield higher intensity, moving the kernel above the memory-bandwidth ridge on modern GPUs (compute-bound).
conditions: FP32 without Tensor Cores; standard tiled algorithm.
nonImplications: Does not imply arbitrarily large tiles are feasible; SMEM and register file limit tile size.
Does not imply this analysis applies unchanged to Tensor Core / TF32 kernels.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Larger BK grows both A tile (BM*BK) and B tile (BK*BN).

misconceptions.claim: 128×128 FP32 accumulators cost 64 KB per thread as registers, forcing spill.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Accumulators are distributed across all threads in the block; per-thread accumulator count is much smaller.

misconceptions.claim: GEMM is always memory-bound regardless of tile size.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Sufficiently large square tiles push arithmetic intensity above the ridge and become compute-bound.

misconceptions.claim: Only Tensor Cores can make GEMM compute-bound.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP32 GEMM with large enough tiles can approach compute-bound; TC just changes the peak FLOP rate.

implementationFacts: SMEM per iter for BM=BN=128, BK=32, FP32: 128*32*4 + 32*128*4 = 32 KB total (both tiles).
A100 FP32 peak ~19.5 TFLOPs; HBM ~1.5 TB/s; ridge point ~13 FLOPs/byte.
